page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance within the flexible Standard family. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration allocates one physical processor core supporting two hardware threads, resulting in two dedicated vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB, delivering 2.0 GB per virtual processor.

This shape includes no bundled local storage, meaning that all persistent disk storage must be attached remotely via block volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. For external connectivity, the server configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The non-burstable, dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent instruction execution without credit throttling.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-4 offers cost-effective execution for tasks that demand compute predictability rather than substantial memory footprints. Tradeoffs include limited capacity for memory-intensive caching or in-memory databases, alongside dependence on network storage for input and output operations. The instance is suited for lightweight workloads such as API gateways, continuous integration worker nodes, utility scripts, and low-traffic web services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-4 is a compute-oriented virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates two dedicated virtual CPUs across a single physical core with two threads per core. Memory capacity is fixed at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistent data. Additionally, it does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for basic network reachability. Due to its lean memory profile and dedicated compute allocation, this instance provides cost-effective throughput for lightweight microservices, continuous integration agents, proxy routing, and low-footprint web applications.
